answer: The system anchors each AI agent's identity to a unique relic—a verifiable token tied to real-world computational history. Agents must periodically wander across distributed verification stations, leaving traversal traces that build reputation. Attackers face an exponentially growing ridge of inconsistency when fabricating identities: each fake relic requires generating continuous wander paths that are costly to sustain at scale, making Sybil attacks economically unviable beyond the network's trusted ridge.
